# PLAN — iteration 1
## Current state assessment
The incumbent uses 16 LUTs and 34 FFs and meets timing, with routed WNS 0.445 ns and WHS 0.208 ns at 10 ns; therefore, promotion requires a verified candidate to use fewer LUTs while retaining timing closure. The CRC update’s eight serial conditional shifts are the main logic target; the top must retain `// @latency 1` and its exact registered, one-slot handshake behavior.

## Hypothesis
Expressing the CRC-16 update as a factored parallel XOR transform may reduce LUT use by exposing the linear CRC equations to Vivado while keeping the existing state and output registers.

## Instruction for generator
Replace the loop-based `crc16_update` function with explicit, factored GF(2) XOR equations for the same 16-bit state and 8-bit data inputs, preserving the `0x1021` polynomial and MSB-first CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE result. Keep the frame-state, output registers, valid/ready logic, synchronous reset priority, and top-level `// @latency 1` behavior unchanged. Preserve acceptance and stall behavior, including stable output payload while blocked; check reset during traffic, consecutive frame endings, and high-bit input patterns.
